tspan.tspan: Tracings of Scheimpflug photography derived from Hermans
but not part of their study.
Layers not visible in the upper an lower parts of the lens are due to photographic limitations imposed by photographing a living person.

Constant Volume of the Human Lens and Decrease in Surface Area of the Capsular Bag during Accommodation: An MRI and Scheimpflug Study.Erik A. Hermans; Petra J. W. Pouwels; Michiel Dubbelman; Joost P. A. Kuijer; Rob G. L. van der
Heijde; Rob M. Heethaar. Investigative Ophthalmology & Visual Science January 2009, Vol.50, 281-289. doi:https://doi.org/10.1167/iovs.08-2124 ”
As the lens stretches for distant vision so do the refracting layers within it, likely causing
complex additional changes to the light path through the lens.
Tracings of Scheimpflug photography of a 20 year old person’s eye
